verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean states the same vanishing-moment step in source-generic form: mass e (⟨f⟩_Y − σ_e · mass e ⟨f⟩_Y) = 0, i.e. the bump is multiplied by the source's own weighted moment rather than by the paper's already-identified defect. The rewriting is routine and is the one the repository itself performs: for e = 2, f = u.thetaResidual, state_radialMoment_eq together with state_angular_moment give mass 2 ⟨E_θ⟩_Y = ε ∂_Z J_θ, so physicalAdjusted P 2 … = ⟨E_θ⟩_Y − σ_θ ε∂_Z J_θ pointwise and the first line follows; for e = 1, f = u.axialResidual, state_axial_moment gives mass 1 ⟨E_z⟩_Y = ε ∂_Z (axialDebtPotential) with axialDebtPotential = axialDefect + pressureCoefficient · pressureDefect, which is the paper's J_z + c_ρ P, giving the second line. The same substitution is carried out inside LocalSignedRequest.physicalBump_improvedClass_of_moment (LocalSignedRequest.lean:1016), applied with e = 2 and e = 1 at GaugeMomentBalances.lean:829 and :857. The bump normalization ∫R^e σ_e dR = 1 is physicalDensity_moment. Two encoding points, neither a mathematical difference: SignedStressPrimitive.mass integrates over all of ℝ rather than the paper's radial half-line (the integrand is compactly supported in the shell √q·[P.a, P.b] ⊂ (0,∞); physicalDensity_positive_moment records the Ioi 0 version for the bump), and the Lean statement is quantified over every exponent e and every smooth shell-supported source, the paper's two lines being the instances e = 2 and e = 1.
